gloss: be far, distant; go far, keep away; remove, put far away; far, distant; distance
summary: To be far off, and to put far off: distance in place, in time, and between man and God. The verb is to be or go far (qal), to remove or keep at a distance (hiphil, piel); the adjective רָחֹק is far, and מֵרָחֹק “from afar”; מֶרְחָק is a distant place. Its fixed opposite is קָרוֹב “near”: “the far and the near” are everyone, and Isaiah's “peace to the far and to the near” the apostles apply to the Gentiles made near by Christ's blood (Isa 57:19; Eph 2:13, 17). The psalmist's cry is that God not be far, the wicked are far from him and from salvation, and Yahweh removes transgressions as far as east from west (Psa 22:2, 12; 119:155; 103:12). The cognates, from Akkadian rêqu to Ge'ez rəḥqa, all mean “be far”.

words.gloss: far, distant, remote; (מֵרָחֹק) from afar, at a distance; long ago
words.summary: Eighty-five times, spelled רָחֹק and רָחוֹק; it is also used as a noun, “distance”, above all with מִן: מֵרָחֹק “from afar, at a distance”. Set against קָרוֹב, “far and near” covers all, of lands, peoples and cities; of God, the far are those who keep away from him.

senses.gloss: far, distant (of a place, land or people)
senses.definition: Of a land, city, road or people: a long way off, at a distance from the speaker or from a named place.

evidence.note: The Gibeonites: “We have come from a land רְחוֹקָה”; and Jos 9:22, “we are very far from you, but you dwell among us”.
“The cities very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations here”: far set against the near cities of the land.
The foreigner who “comes from a land רְחוֹקָה because of your name” (also 2Ch 6:32).
Hezekiah: “They have come from a land רְחוֹקָה, from Babylon.”
One “on a road רְחֹקָה” keeps a later Passover, as one who is unclean.
“Better a neighbour near (קָרוֹב) than a brother far (רָחוֹק).”
Laish was “far from the Sidonians”, so none came to its help (Jdg 18:28).
“We are separated on the wall, a man far from his brother.”
“The man has gone on a far road.”
“The far coastlands that have not heard my report.”
He will judge “strong nations far away”.
Sold “to the Sabeans, to a far nation”.

senses.definition: With מִן, adverbially: seen, standing or heard at a distance; often of those who keep their distance, by fear, grief, reverence or estrangement.

evidence.note: “On the third day Abraham lifted his eyes and saw the place מֵרָחֹק.”
“They saw him מֵרָחֹק, and before he came near (יִקְרַב) to them they conspired against him.”
His sister “stationed herself מֵרָחֹק to know what would be done to him”.
“The people stood מֵרָחֹק, and Moses drew near (נִגַּשׁ) to the thick darkness where God was”; also Exo 20:18.
The elders “shall bow down מֵרָחֹק, and Moses alone shall come near”.
The tax collector “standing at a distance (μακρόθεν; Peshitta מֵנ רֻוחקָא)” would not lift his eyes to heaven.
“My loved ones and my friends stand aloof from my plague, and my kinsmen stand מֵרָחֹק.”
His friends “lifted their eyes מֵרָחוֹק and did not recognise him”.
Fifty of the sons of the prophets “stood opposite מֵרָחוֹק”.
David stood on the top of the hill מֵרָחֹק, “a great space between them”.
“There shall be a distance (רָחוֹק) between you and it, about two thousand cubits; do not come near it”: the word as a noun.
“You understand my thought מֵרָחוֹק.”
The horse “smells the battle מֵרָחוֹק”.
The shout “was heard as far as מֵרָחוֹק”; also Neh 12:43.
“From afar Yahweh appeared to me: with everlasting love I have loved you.”
“Your sons shall come from afar”; also Isa 43:6; 49:12; 60:9.
“Yahweh will bring a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth”; also Isa 5:26.
“Behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity”; also Jer 46:27.
To the exiles: “Remember Yahweh from afar, and let Jerusalem come up on your heart.”

senses.gloss: the far and the near: all, everyone
senses.definition: Paired with קָרוֹב, the far and the near together are the whole: every people, place or person, wherever they are. Isa 57:19, peace to the far and the near, the apostles read of the Gentiles and Israel.

evidence.note: “Peace, peace לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב, says Yahweh, and I will heal him.”
Isa 57:19 expounded: Christ “came and preached peace to you who were far off (μακράν; Peshitta לרַחִיקֵא) and to those near”, the far being the Gentiles of Eph 2:11–13.
“You who once were far off have become near by the blood of Christ.”
“The promise is to you and your children, and to all who are far off (Peshitta דּרַחִיקִין), as many as the Lord our God will call.”
“Hear, you far ones (רְחוֹקִים), what I have done; and know, you near ones, my might.”
The gods of the peoples “near to you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other”.
Captives in the land of the enemy, “far or near”; also 2Ch 6:36.
Mordecai's letters to all the Jews in the provinces, “the near and the far”.
“To all Israel, the near and the far, in all the lands where you have driven them.”
“The near and the far from you will mock you.”
“The far shall die by the plague, and the near shall fall by the sword.”
“All the kings of the north, the near and the far.”
“All the cities of the land of Moab, the far and the near.”
“And far ones (רְחוֹקִים) shall come and build in the temple of Yahweh.”
“Listen, coastlands, and attend, peoples from afar.”

senses.definition: Of the wicked: far from Yahweh, from righteousness and from salvation; near to God in the mouth, far from him within. And of Yahweh, who is far from the wicked but hears the righteous.

evidence.note: “Yahweh is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.”
“Salvation is far from the wicked, for they have not sought your statutes”; set against Psa 119:151, “you are near, Yahweh”.
“You are near (קָרוֹב) in their mouth, and far from their kidneys.”
“Listen to me, stubborn of heart, הָרְחוֹקִים מִצְּדָקָה”; answered in Isa 46:13, “I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far”.
“Justice is turned back, and righteousness stands afar.”
To the scribe who answered wisely: “You are not far (Peshitta רַחִיק) from the kingdom of God.”

senses.gloss: far off (of God, to the sufferer)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh, as the afflicted feel his absence: standing far off, far from saving. The prayer is that he come near.

evidence.note: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? רָחוֹק מִישׁוּעָתִי”: far from my salvation; the cry Jesus took up on the cross (Mat 27:46).
“Why, Yahweh, do you stand afar (בְּרָחוֹק)? Why do you hide in times of trouble?”
“Am I a God at hand, says Yahweh, and not a God afar off?” He is near to see all and far to rule all (Jer 23:24).
Paul: men should seek God, “though he is not far (Peshitta רַחִיק) from each one of us”.

senses.definition: Of time: long past, or far in the future.

evidence.note: “Have you not heard? לְמֵרָחוֹק I did it; from days of old (מִימֵי קֶדֶם) I formed it”: parallel to “days of old” (also Isa 37:26).
“You did not regard him who formed it מֵרָחוֹק.”
“Counsels מֵרָחוֹק, faithfulness and truth.”
“You have spoken also of your servant's house לְמֵרָחוֹק”: for a great while to come, the promise of an everlasting house and kingdom (2Sa 7:16); also 1Ch 17:17.
“The vision he sees is for many days, and he prophesies לְעִתִּים רְחוֹקוֹת”: for far-off times.
“Far off is that which has been, and deep, deep: who can find it out?”
“I said, I will be wise, but it was far from me.”

senses.definition: With מִן of comparison: far above, out of reach of.

evidence.note: “A woman of worth, who can find? Her price is far beyond (וְרָחֹק מִן) pearls.”

evidence.locator: Isa.57.19, לָרָחוֹק → μακράν; Psa.22.2; 119.155; Pro.15.29; Zec.6.15; Deu.30.11 → μακράν; μακράν renders the root ×33

evidence.note: “Peace to you who were far off (τοῖς μακράν)”: the Septuagint's word in Isa 57:19.

evidence.locator: Exo.2.4; 20.21; Psa.10.1; 38.12, רָחֹק → μακρόθεν; Psa.138.6, מִמֶּרְחָק → μακρόθεν; μακρόθεν renders the root ×28

evidence.note: The tax collector “standing μακρόθεν”, as Israel stood afar at Sinai (Exo 20:21).
“Seeing Jesus μακρόθεν, he ran and worshipped him.”

evidence.locator: πόρρω renders the root ×6, πόρρωθεν ×13 (Isa.33.13; Jer.23.23; Job.39.25)

evidence.note: Isa 29:13 quoted: “their heart is far (πόρρω) from me”; the Peshitta writes רַחִיק.

opposites.note: “Near”: the fixed pair, “the far and the near”.

phrases.gloss: the far and the near: all

words.gloss: be far, go far, keep away; remove, put far away; extend
words.summary: Fifty-seven times: the qal to be or go far, the hiphil and piel to put far away (and the hiphil also, without object, to go far). Distance here is often estrangement: friends keep away from the afflicted, Israel goes far from Yahweh, and the sufferer begs God not to be far. Its opposite is קָרַב “come near” (Psa 22:12; 119:150; Isa 54:14; Pro 5:8).

stems.gloss: be far, be too far; go far, keep away; (of God, help) be far

senses.definition: Of a place or a boundary: to be a long way off.

evidence.note: “If the place that Yahweh your God chooses to put his name there is too far (יִרְחַק) from you”; also Deu 14:24, where the road is too long to carry the tithe.
“As far (כִּרְחֹק) as the east is from the west”: the infinitive as a measure of distance.
“A day for building your walls; in that day the boundary (חֹק) will be far”: the border pushed far out.
Zion will be too narrow for her people, “and those who swallowed you up will be far away”.

senses.gloss: go far, keep away, hold aloof
senses.definition: Of persons: to go away from someone or something and keep away; of friends, to shun the afflicted; of the wise, to keep clear of what is evil.

evidence.note: “All the brothers of the poor hate him; how much more do his friends go far from him!”
“They abhor me, they keep far from me, and do not spare to spit in my face.”
“From a false word תִּרְחָק, and do not kill the innocent and righteous.”
“Thorns and snares are in the way of the crooked; he who guards his soul keeps far from them.”
“Be far from oppression, for you shall not fear; and from terror, for it shall not come near (תִקְרַב) you.”
“A time to embrace, and a time לִרְחֹק מֵחַבֵּק”: to keep far from embracing.
“The counsel of the wicked is far from me”; also Job 22:18.
“He did not delight in blessing, and it went far from him.”

senses.definition: Of Israel, its fathers or its Levites: to go away from Yahweh after idols; and of the wicked, to be far from his law.

evidence.note: “What wrong did your fathers find in me, that they went far from me, and went after emptiness, and became empty?”
“The Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray (תָּעוּ), who went astray from me after their idols.”
“They draw near (קָרְבוּ) who pursue evil; they are far from your law.”
The men of Jerusalem said of the exiles, “Go far from Yahweh; to us the land is given as a possession”; Yahweh answers that he has been a sanctuary to them in the lands (Ezk 11:16).
The abominations of the house of Israel “to go far from my sanctuary”: whether the people's going or Yahweh's driven from it, the abominations put distance between them.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, his help, justice or salvation: to be far from the one in need; in prayer, “do not be far from me”.

evidence.note: “Be not far from me, for trouble is near (קְרוֹבָה), for there is none to help.”
“But you, Yahweh, be not far; my strength, hasten to help me.”
“Do not forsake (תַּעַזְבֵנִי) me, Yahweh; my God, be not far from me”: parallel to forsake.
“Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not overtake us”; and Isa 59:11, “for salvation, but it is far from us”.
“I bring near (קֵרַבְתִּי) my righteousness; it shall not be far, and my salvation shall not delay.”
“A comforter who would restore my soul is far from me.”
The fool's sons “are far from safety”.

stems.gloss: remove, put far away; go far; (infinitive הַרְחֵק) at a distance

senses.definition: To make something or someone far off: to put away sin or falsehood, to drive a people from its land, to estrange friends.

evidence.note: “As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed (הִרְחִיק) our transgressions from us.”
“Put away (הָסֵר) from you a crooked mouth, and devious lips put far (הַרְחֵק) from you”: parallel to the hiphil of סוּר.
“If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and let not unrighteousness dwell in your tents”; also Job 22:23.
“Emptiness and a lying word put far from me.”
“Folly is bound in the heart of a boy; the rod of discipline will drive it far from him.”
“You have put lover and friend far from me”; and Psa 88:9, “you have put my acquaintances far from me, you have made me an abomination to them”.
“He has put my brothers far from me, and my acquaintances are wholly estranged (זָרוּ) from me.”
“Withdraw your hand far from me.”
The false prophets prophesy a lie “to remove you far from your land, and I will drive you out and you will perish”.
“Though I removed them far among the nations … yet I have been to them a little sanctuary in the lands.”
The sons of Judah sold to the Greeks “to remove them far from their border”.
“I will remove far from you the northerner (הַצְּפוֹנִי), and drive him into a land dry and desolate”: the invader from the north.

senses.gloss: go far; keep at a distance; (הַרְחֵק) far off
senses.definition: With no object: to go a long way, or keep one's distance; the infinitive הַרְחֵק as an adverb, “at a distance”.

evidence.note: “They had gone out of the city and had not gone far (לֹא הִרְחִיקוּ).”
“They had gone far from the house of Micah.”
Pharaoh: “Only you shall not go very far (הַרְחֵק לֹא־תַרְחִיקוּ).”
“Do not go very far from the city.”
“Behold, I would wander far off (אַרְחִיק נְדֹד), I would lodge in the wilderness.”
“Keep your way far from her, and do not come near (תִּקְרַב) the door of her house.”
Hagar “sat down opposite, הַרְחֵק, about a bowshot”.
The tent of meeting pitched outside the camp, “far off (הַרְחֵק) from the camp”.
The waters stood in one heap “very far off (הַרְחֵק מְאֹד), at Adam”.

stems.gloss: send far, remove; extend; (of the heart) keep far

senses.definition: To send off to a distance: of Yahweh's exile of the people, and of Israel putting its idolatry away.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has removed man far away (וְרִחַק), and the forsaken places are many in the land”: exile.
“Now let them put far their whoredom and the corpses of their kings from me, and I will dwell in their midst for ever.”

senses.definition: To push far out: to widen a land's borders.

evidence.note: “You have increased the nation, Yahweh … you have extended (רִחַקְתָּ) all the ends of the land.”

senses.definition: Of the heart, without object: to hold itself far from Yahweh while the mouth draws near.

evidence.note: “This people draws near (נִגַּשׁ) with its mouth and honours me with its lips, but its heart רִחַק מִמֶּנִּי.”
Jesus quotes Isa 29:13 of the Pharisees' traditions: “their heart is far (πόρρω; Peshitta רַחִיק) from me”; also Mrk 7:6.

evidence.locator: Exo.23.7, תִּרְחָק → ἀποστήσῃ; Psa.22.12; 35.22; 38.22, אַל־תִּרְחַק → μὴ ἀποστῇς; Isa.59.9, רָחַק → ἀπέστη

evidence.note: “An evil heart of unbelief, in departing (ἀποστῆναι) from the living God”: the going far from God of Jer 2:5.

parallels.note: “Forsake”: to be far is to forsake.
Hiphil “put away”, beside the hiphil “put far”.
“Go astray”: going far from Yahweh after idols.
“Abhor”: those who keep far from the afflicted loathe him.

words.summary: Eighteen times, with the מ- of place: in אֶרֶץ מֶרְחָק “a land of distance”, in מִמֶּרְחָק “from afar”, and in the plural, the far places of the earth. In 2Sa 15:17 בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָק “the far house” may be a place name, the last house of the city.

senses.gloss: a distant place; (אֶרֶץ מֶרְחָק) a far land
senses.definition: A place a long way off, most often “a land of distance”, from which armies, goods or news come.

evidence.note: “They come from a land of distance, from the end of the heavens, Yahweh and the weapons of his indignation.”
“Watchers come from the far land (מֵאֶרֶץ הַמֶּרְחָק).”
“Calling a bird of prey from the east, the man of my counsel from a far land.”
“Sweet cane from a far land.”
“As cold water to a weary soul, so is good news from a far land.”
“The cry of the daughter of my people from a land of distances (מַרְחַקִּים).”
“They stood at בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָק”: the far house, the last house before the Kidron.

senses.definition: With מִן: from a distance, as מֵרָחֹק.

evidence.note: “Though Yahweh is high, he regards the lowly, and the proud he knows from afar.”
“Behold, the name of Yahweh comes from afar, burning with his anger.”
“What will you do in the day of visitation, in the storm that comes from afar?”
“I bring a nation upon you from afar, house of Israel.”
“Declare it in the coastlands afar off: he who scattered Israel will gather him.”
“You sent for men to come from afar.”
“She brings her food from afar.”
Rebuked, the nations “flee far off”.

senses.gloss: (plural) far places, the ends of the earth
senses.definition: In the plural: the far reaches of the earth, and those who live there; the wide land of the king.

evidence.note: “Give ear, all the far places (מֶרְחַקֵּי) of the earth.”
“I will sow them among the peoples, and in far places (בַמֶּרְחַקִּים) they shall remember me, and they shall live … and return.”
“Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty; they shall behold a land of far distances (אֶרֶץ מַרְחַקִּים)”: the wide land of the king's reign.

evidence.locator: Psa.138.6, מִמֶּרְחָק → μακρόθεν; μακρόθεν renders מֶרְחָק ×7

words.summary: Once, as a noun with a suffix: “those far from you”, the verbal adjective of the qal, set against the psalmist's nearness to God.

senses.gloss: those who are far from you (God)
senses.definition: Those who keep themselves far from God; the next words name them the unfaithful, and the next verse sets them against “the nearness of God”.

evidence.note: “For behold, רְחֵקֶיךָ shall perish; you destroy everyone who goes whoring from you.”
“But for me, the nearness of God (קִרֲבַת אֱלֹהִים) is good.”

words.summary: Once in scripture's Aramaic, in Darius's decree: the officials beyond the River are to keep away from the house of God and let the work go on.

senses.definition: With הֲוָה and מִן: be far from, keep away from, so as not to hinder.

evidence.note: “Now, Tattenai … and your companions, רַחִיקִין הֲווֹ מִן־תַּמָּה”: be far from there.
“Let the work of this house of God alone”: what keeping far means.

cognates.gloss: be(come) distant, go far away, remove; (rūqu) distant, far; distance
cognates.note: Akkadian loses the guttural and colours the vowel (rêqu beside רָחַק, as rēmu beside רֶחֶם); it keeps ḫ as ḫ, so it shows that the letter was not ḫ. The verb and adjective match the Hebrew verb and רָחֹק.

evidence.note: “be(come) distant; go far away; remove; step back”.
“distant; far; far apart; distance; long; deep”.

cognates.note: Keret: the imperative “go away” from the king's house. The noun mrḥq(t) is formed as מֶרְחָק, and “from (the) distance” is used as מִמֶּרְחָק. Ugaritic writes ḥ, not ḫ.

evidence.locator: x000001470, mrḥqt [distance] N; x000001460, mrḥq [distance] N

evidence.note: rḥq 1.14 III 28, imperative “to withdraw oneself” (comparing Hebrew rāḥaq, Akkadian rêqu); mrḥqtm 2.64:15 “from … distance(s)”, comparing Hebrew mē-rāḥōq Exo 2:4.

cognates.gloss: be far off, be distant, go far, keep away, depart; (causative) put far away, remove, estrange, delay; (rəḥq) distance
cognates.note: The same range as the Hebrew, stem for stem: the simple stem “be far, go far, keep away” and the causative “put far, remove”, of place and of time (keep far, delay). Ge'ez ሐ shows ḥ behind ח.

evidence.note: “be far off, be distant, go some distance (from), go far, keep away, be remote, depart, abstain, desist (from), withdraw”; ʾarḥaqa “keep afar, set apart, remove, put at a distance, reject, estrange, put off, delay”; rəḥq “distance, remoteness”.
ርሕቀ “procul abesse, remotum esse, distare … longe recedere, discedere”; አርሐቀ “procul amovere, removere … abalienare”.

cognates.note: Old South Arabian inscriptions pair it with qrb “near” as Hebrew does: protection from “an enemy who is far or near”, and expeditions “near and far”. South Arabian ḥ shows ḥ behind ח.

evidence.note: adj “far (bn from)”; R 3929/13 šnʾm drḥq wqrb “an enemy who is far or near”; J 737/4 šnʾm rḥqm wqrbm.

cognates.note: Listed in the Proto-Semitic root set; not yet checked in a Punic edition or Krahmalkov.

evidence.locator: SEM000358 rḥq [distant] V, PUN001874 rḥq [far] A

cognates.gloss: be far; (pael, aphel) remove, keep off, reject; loathe, abominate; (rāḥīq) far, distant
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targums: the same verb for the Hebrew (Targ. Pro 19:7; Psa 103:12; Job 21:16), and the causative stems for putting away; but “keep off” also becomes “loathe”, and the passive participle מְרָחַק “abominable” renders Hebrew נִתְעָב and פִּגּוּל, distance as rejection, as in Job 30:10 and Psa 88:9.

evidence.locator: s.v. רְחֵק (ch.), citing Targ. Prov. XIX, 7; Targ. Ps. CIII, 12; Af. Targ. Ex. XXXIII, 7; Targ. Is. VI, 12; Pa. Targ. Job XI, 14; Targ. Deut. VII, 26 (loathe)
s.v. רָחִיק II, citing Targ. Deut. XXIX, 21; Targ. Jer. XII, 2
evidence.note: “far, distant, removed”.

evidence.locator: s.v. מְרָחַק, citing Targ. Job XV, 16 (h. text נתעב); Targ. O. Lev. VII, 18 (h. text פגול)
evidence.note: “abominable, unclean”.

cognates.gloss: keep away from, remove, depart; far, distant, remote; a far place, (men ruḥqā) from afar
cognates.note: The Peshitta's word for the New Testament's “far”: the Gentiles “who were far” (Eph 2:13, 17), “all who are far” (Act 2:39), the heart “far from me” (Mat 15:8), and men ruḥqā “from afar” (Mat 26:58; Luk 18:13).

evidence.locator: root 1755 RKX; lexemes 3006 ROKXA (far place; from afar), 3007 RK;XA (far; distant; remote), 3008 RKX (keep away from; remove; depart)

doctrine.statement: Yahweh promised “peace, peace to the far and to the near” (Isa 57:19), and foretold that “far ones shall come and build in the temple of Yahweh” (Zec 6:15). Paul names the far: Gentiles, “strangers to the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world” (Eph 2:12), who “have become near by the blood of Christ” (Eph 2:13), to whom Christ preached Isaiah's peace (Eph 2:17); and Peter offers the promise “to all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God will call” (Act 2:39). So the Gentiles are brought near not to a separate hope but to Israel's: once strangers to the covenants of the promise, the far are now “fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God” (Eph 2:19).

Yahweh “has removed our transgressions from us as far as the east is from the west” (Psa 103:12), in a psalm that begins “who forgives all your iniquities” (Psa 103:3) and grounds it in his mercy to those who fear him, remembering that “we are dust” (Psa 103:11, 14). Forgiveness is God putting sin away from the sinner, not the sinner's own doing; what is asked of man is to put iniquity far from himself in turn (Job 11:14; 22:23; Pro 4:24).

Distance from God is the state of the wicked: Yahweh is far from them, and salvation is far from them, because they have not sought his statutes (Pro 15:29; Psa 119:155); a people may honour him with its lips while its heart is far from him, which Jesus applied to worship by the commandments of men (Isa 29:13; Mat 15:8–9). And it ends in death: “those far from you shall perish”, while “the nearness of God is good” (Psa 73:27–28). The wicked perish; nothing in these verses gives them a life apart from God.

On the cross Jesus cried the opening of Psalm 22, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” (Mat 27:46), whose next words are “far from my salvation” (Psa 22:2). The psalm prays “be not far from me” (Psa 22:12, 20) and ends answered: “he has not hidden his face from him, but when he cried to him, he heard” (Psa 22:25), and then “I will declare your name to my brothers”, which Hebrews puts in Christ's mouth (Psa 22:23; Heb 2:12). Hebrews says the same: in the days of his flesh he prayed with strong crying and tears “to him who was able to save him from death, and was heard” (Heb 5:7). A man who could feel God far off and be saved from death is the Son of God as scripture presents him, raised by his Father.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19. BDB keys: t.cf.aa (verb, 57), t.cf.ab (רָחֵק, Psa 73:27), t.cf.ac (רָחֹק, 85), t.cf.ad (מֶרְחָק, 18) and the zero-token cross-reference m.dl.ac on מֶרְחָק; xt.aj.ab (Biblical Aramaic רְחִיק, Ezr 6:6) on the Aramaic word, keyed by its own root רחיק. The Aramaic root key xt.aj.aa is left unclaimed, as other entries leave theirs. 2Sa 15:17 הַמֶּרְחָק is also filed under b.bp.bf (בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָק, possibly a place name), left with that key. Psa 103:12 has both the qal infinitive כִּרְחֹק and the hiphil הִרְחִיק, cited under each. Isa 29:13 רִחַק is pointed piel but has no object (the heart “keeps far”), filed as a piel sense. Ezk 8:6 לְרָחֳקָה: whether the people go far from the sanctuary or Yahweh is made to go far is open; filed under qal “go far from Yahweh”. No personal name is formed from the root: TIPNR has only the place בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָק (2Sa 15:17) and the psalm title יוֹנַת אֵלֶם רְחֹקִים (Psa 56:1), neither a person. Cognates: Arabic has no root rḥq “far” (Arabic uses baʿuda); Lane's رحيق “choice wine” is not entered, and the suggestion that it means “wine from afar” rests on nothing in Lane. Ugaritic, Ge'ez and Sabaic all write ḥ; Akkadian's loss of the guttural with e-colouring excludes ḫ. The Punic rḥq is from Anderson–Moser only; Krahmalkov's text layer did not yield the entry (OCR), so it is not yet checked. Payne Smith not consulted for Syriac. Open questions: (1) Jol 2:20 הַצְּפוֹנִי read plainly as the invader from the north; the hiphil note says only that. (2) Isa 33:17 אֶרֶץ מַרְחַקִּים read as the wide land of the king's reign rather than “a land far off”. (3) Job 36:3 לְמֵרָחוֹק and Psa 56:1 (the title “a silent dove of far ones”) and Psa 65:6 (“the far seas”) are not cited.
